q18315.en: On a carriageway of the type shown, you may overtake even on a bend.

explain.short: Here you have two lanes in your direction. You can overtake on a bend without going into the lanes of oncoming traffic.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'anche in curva' (even on a bend) sounds dangerous, but with two lanes per direction it is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes your way: overtaking on a bend is allowed

q18316.en: The carriageway of the type shown is two-way.

explain.short: The picture has two lanes for each direction on the same carriageway. Traffic goes both ways.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso di circolazione' means two-way traffic: two directions on one carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes up, two lanes down: two-way traffic

q18317.en: On an out-of-town carriageway of the type shown, the inner lanes are, as a rule, reserved for overtaking.

explain.short: Outside towns you drive in the right lane. The inner lanes, next to the centre line, are for overtaking.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) and 'corsie interne' (inner lanes, near the centre) are the key words.

sceneParams.caption: Outside towns: right lane to drive, inner lane to overtake

q18318.en: On a carriageway of the type shown, you cannot make a U-turn.

explain.short: The two directions are divided by a continuous line that you cannot cross. A U-turn here would also cut across four lanes of traffic.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' means U-turn: turning round to go back the other way.

sceneParams.caption: Continuous centre line: no U-turn here

q18319.en: On an out-of-town carriageway of the type shown, you may overtake either on the right or on the left, as you like.

explain.short: Overtaking is done on the left. Overtaking on the right is allowed only in special cases, for example when the car ahead is turning left.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'indifferentemente' means 'it makes no difference': wrong, the side is not your free choice.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake on the LEFT, not on whichever side you like
lines: On the right: only special cases

q18320.en: On an out-of-town carriageway of the type shown, you may always drive in parallel rows.

explain.short: Outside towns you keep to the right lane. Driving side by side is allowed only when traffic is very heavy, not always.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap word: parallel rows are only for heavy traffic.

sceneParams.caption: Side by side only in heavy traffic, not always
lines: Side by side: only heavy traffic

keywords.en: to drive in parallel rows (side by side)

q18321.en: On a carriageway of the type shown, we may start overtaking even if the driver behind has already started the same manoeuvre.

explain.short: If the car behind is already overtaking, you must wait. Pulling out would put you in its path.
explain.rule: On a carriageway with two lanes per direction, you keep right for normal driving and use the inner lane to overtake, always on the left.
explain.trap: 'anche se' (even if) makes it sound fine; but 'ha già iniziato' (has already started) means you must wait.

sceneParams.caption: Driver behind is already overtaking: you wait

q18322.en: On the road shown, in each direction, the right lane is, as a rule, for normal driving.

explain.short: You always drive as far right as possible. So the right lane is the normal driving lane.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'marcia ordinaria' means normal driving (not overtaking); 'di norma' means as a rule.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane = normal driving

q18323.en: The road shown has three lanes in each direction.

explain.short: Count the lanes on one side of the central line: there are three. The other side also has three.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'per ogni senso di marcia' means 'for each direction': 3 + 3, not 3 in total.

sceneParams.caption: 3 lanes each way: 6 lanes in total

q18324.en: On the road shown, in each direction, the centre and left lanes are, as a rule, for overtaking.

explain.short: Normal driving is in the right lane. The centre and left lanes are used to overtake.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'corsie di centro e di sinistra' (centre and left lanes) are both for overtaking.

sceneParams.caption: Centre and left lanes: for overtaking
sceneParams.it: corsie di centro e di sinistra

keywords.it: corsie di centro e di sinistra

q18325.en: The road shown has one carriageway.

explain.short: The two directions are divided only by painted lines, not by a traffic divider. So it is a single carriageway.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'una carreggiata' (one carriageway): painted lines do not make two carriageways.

sceneParams.caption: Only lines in the middle: ONE carriageway

q18326.en: On the road shown, in each direction, the centre lane is, as a rule, for normal driving.

explain.short: Normal driving is in the right lane. The centre lane is for overtaking.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'corsia di centro' (centre lane) is an overtaking lane, not the normal lane.

sceneParams.caption: Centre lane is for overtaking; normal driving is right

q18327.en: On the road shown, in each direction, the right lane is, as a rule, for overtaking.

explain.short: The right lane is for normal driving. You overtake using the centre or left lane.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'corsia di destra' + 'sorpasso' is the swap: the right lane is for normal driving.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane is for normal driving, not overtaking

q18328.en: The road shown has two carriageways.

explain.short: The two directions are divided only by painted lines. Two carriageways would need a physical divider (spartitraffico) between them.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate' (two carriageways) is wrong: lines alone make one carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Only lines in the middle: one carriageway, not two

q18329.en: On the road shown, in each direction, the left lane is, as a rule, for normal driving.

explain.short: The left lane is for overtaking. Normal driving is in the right lane.
explain.rule: With three lanes per direction, the right lane is for normal driving; the centre and left lanes are for overtaking.
explain.trap: 'corsia di sinistra' (left lane) is an overtaking lane, not the normal driving lane.

sceneParams.caption: Left lane is for overtaking; normal driving is right

q18330.en: The road shown has three carriageways.

explain.short: Two traffic dividers (spartitraffico) split the road into three parts. Each part is a carriageway.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: Count the dividers, not the lines: 'tre carreggiate' (three carriageways) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Two dividers: three carriageways

q18331.en: The road shown has eight lanes.

explain.short: Side carriageways: 2 lanes each. Central carriageway: 4 lanes. 2 + 4 + 2 = 8.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'otto corsie' (eight lanes): count lanes, not carriageways.

sceneParams.caption: 2 + 4 + 2 = 8 lanes

q18332.en: On the road shown, the side carriageways are, as a rule, one-way.

explain.short: Each side carriageway has two lanes going in the same direction. So each one is one-way.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate laterali' are the side carriageways; 'senso unico' means one-way.

sceneParams.caption: Side carriageways: one-way

q18333.en: On the road shown, the central carriageway is, as a rule, two-way.

explain.short: The central carriageway has four lanes: two go one way and two go the other way.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'carreggiata centrale' (central carriageway) is two-way; do not confuse it with a 'corsia' (lane).

sceneParams.caption: Central carriageway: two lanes each way

q18334.en: The road shown, as a rule, allows overtaking even on a bend.

explain.short: Every carriageway here has at least two lanes per direction. So you can overtake on a bend without entering oncoming lanes.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'anche in curva' (even on a bend) sounds risky, but with two lanes your way it is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes your way: overtaking on a bend is allowed

q18335.en: The road shown has four carriageways, all one-way.

explain.short: There are only two dividers, so there are three carriageways. The central one is two-way.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'quattro carreggiate' (four) and 'tutte a senso unico' (all one-way) are both wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Three carriageways, and the central one is two-way

q18336.en: The road shown has eight carriageways.

explain.short: Eight is the number of lanes, not carriageways. There are three carriageways.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'otto carreggiate' mixes up 'corsie' (lanes) and 'carreggiate' (carriageways).

sceneParams.caption: 8 lanes, but only 3 carriageways

q18337.en: The road shown, as a rule, has two two-way carriageways.

explain.short: Only the central carriageway is two-way. The two side carriageways are one-way.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate a doppio senso' (two two-way carriageways) is wrong: only one is two-way.

sceneParams.caption: Only the central carriageway is two-way

q18338.en: The road shown has three lanes.

explain.short: Three is the number of carriageways. The lanes are eight.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'tre corsie' mixes up 'corsie' (lanes) and 'carreggiate' (carriageways).

sceneParams.caption: 3 carriageways, but 8 lanes

q18339.en: On the road shown, the central lane is two-way.

explain.short: A single lane always carries traffic in one direction. It is the central CARRIAGEWAY that is two-way.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'corsia centrale' (central lane) replaces 'carreggiata centrale' (central carriageway): that changes everything.

sceneParams.caption: The central CARRIAGEWAY is two-way, not a lane

q18340.en: On the side carriageways of the road shown, U-turns are, as a rule, allowed.

explain.short: The side carriageways are one-way. A U-turn would make you drive against the traffic.
explain.rule: A carriageway is separated by a traffic divider; a lane is separated by painted lines. Here: 3 carriageways, 8 lanes.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' (U-turn) is not possible on a 'senso unico' (one-way) carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: One-way carriageway: no U-turn

q18341.en: A pedestrian crossing is marked with parallel white stripes.

explain.short: The zebra crossing is painted as wide white stripes, parallel to each other and to the road.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'strisce bianche parallele' (parallel white stripes): white, not yellow.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra crossing: parallel white stripes

q18342.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway on which vehicles may not stop.

explain.short: Stopping on the crossing would block pedestrians and hide them from other drivers. So it is forbidden.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'fermata' means a short stop (e.g. to let someone out): it is forbidden on the crossing.

sceneParams.caption: No stopping on a pedestrian crossing

q18343.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on the stripes.

explain.short: When a pedestrian is crossing on the stripes, you must slow down and let them cross first.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'dare la precedenza' means to give way: the pedestrian on the stripes goes first.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian on the stripes: you give way

q18344.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway meant for pedestrians who are crossing.

explain.short: The crossing is where pedestrians cross the road. It is part of the carriageway, where cars also drive.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'destinata al transito dei pedoni' (meant for pedestrians passing): it is still part of the 'carreggiata'.

sceneParams.caption: Part of the carriageway where pedestrians cross

q18345.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway on which vehicles may not park.

explain.short: You cannot leave your car on the crossing. Parking there is forbidden, just like stopping.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'sosta' means parking (leaving the car for a longer time): forbidden on the crossing.

sceneParams.caption: No parking on a pedestrian crossing

q18346.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the road separated from the carriageway by a yellow line.

explain.short: The crossing is inside the carriageway and is marked with white stripes. Nothing yellow separates it.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'separata dalla carreggiata' and 'striscia gialla' (yellow line) are both wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Crossing is IN the carriageway, with white stripes

q18347.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway closed to vehicle traffic.

explain.short: Cars may drive over the crossing. They only have to give way to pedestrians who are crossing.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'vietata al transito dei veicoli' (closed to vehicles) is wrong: you may drive over it.

sceneParams.caption: Cars may drive over it, giving way to pedestrians

q18348.en: A pedestrian crossing is not part of the carriageway.

explain.short: The crossing is painted on the carriageway itself, where cars drive. So it is part of it.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'non fa parte' (is not part of) is the trap: it IS part of the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: The crossing IS part of the carriageway

q18349.en: A pedestrian crossing is located outside the carriageway and is meant for pedestrians passing.

explain.short: Pedestrians do use it, but it is not outside the carriageway: it is painted on it.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: Half right, half wrong: 'al di fuori della carreggiata' (outside the carriageway) makes it false.

sceneParams.caption: The crossing is ON the carriageway, not outside

q18350.en: A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway where vehicles may stop but not park.

explain.short: On a pedestrian crossing both stopping and parking are forbidden.
explain.rule: A pedestrian crossing is part of the carriageway, with white stripes: give way to pedestrians, no stopping and no parking on it.
explain.trap: 'consentita la fermata' (stopping allowed) is the trap: stopping is forbidden too.

sceneParams.caption: No stopping AND no parking on the crossing

q18351.en: Main out-of-town roads have separate carriageways.

explain.short: A main out-of-town road has two carriageways, one for each direction, divided by a traffic divider.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate separate' (separate carriageways) is a must for this road type.

sceneParams.caption: Separate carriageways, one per direction

q18352.en: Main out-of-town roads have dedicated rest areas.

explain.short: These roads must have service areas with space where you can stop and rest. You cannot just stop on the road.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'apposite aree di sosta' means special areas built for stopping.

sceneParams.caption: Dedicated rest areas along the road
lines: Stop there, not on the road

q18353.en: A main out-of-town road has no level junctions crossing it.

explain.short: Other roads do not cross it at the same level. They pass above or below it.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'incroci a raso' means level junctions (roads crossing at the same height): there are none.

sceneParams.caption: No level junctions: other roads go over or under

q18354.en: Main out-of-town roads are marked by start and end road signs.

explain.short: A sign tells you where the main out-of-town road starts, and another where it ends.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'inizio e fine' means start and end: both are signposted.

sceneParams.caption: Start and end signs mark this road

q18355.en: Only some categories of motor vehicles may travel on main out-of-town roads.

explain.short: These roads are for certain motor vehicles only. Mopeds, light quadricycles, bikes and pedestrians are not allowed.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'solo alcune categorie' (only some categories) is correct: not every vehicle may enter.

sceneParams.caption: Only some motor vehicles: no mopeds, no bikes

q18356.en: On main out-of-town roads you may find grade-separated intersections (junctions).

explain.short: Junctions here are built on different levels, with ramps, bridges or underpasses.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'livelli sfalsati' means different levels: junctions with roads above and below.

sceneParams.caption: Junctions on different levels, with ramps

q18357.en: Main out-of-town roads have acceleration lanes for entering.

explain.short: When you join the road, you first use an acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'corsie di accelerazione' are acceleration lanes, used to enter safely.

sceneParams.caption: Join using the acceleration lane

q18358.en: On main out-of-town roads you may drive at a maximum speed of 130 km/h.

explain.short: The general limit on main out-of-town roads is 110 km/h. 130 km/h is the motorway limit.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: '130 km/h' is the motorway number; here it is 110 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Limit here is 110 km/h; 130 is for motorways

q18359.en: Main out-of-town roads are marked with green signage.

explain.short: Direction signs on main out-of-town roads are blue. Green signs are for motorways.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'segnaletica verde' (green signs) belongs to motorways, not to these roads.

sceneParams.caption: Blue signs here; green is for motorways

q18360.en: Main out-of-town roads may have a single carriageway.

explain.short: A main out-of-town road must have separate carriageways. A single carriageway is never enough.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'un'unica carreggiata' (a single carriageway) is wrong: they must be separate.

sceneParams.caption: Must have separate carriageways, never just one

q18361.en: On main out-of-town roads you may drive at the same maximum speed as on motorways.

explain.short: Motorways allow 130 km/h. Main out-of-town roads allow only 110 km/h.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'stessa velocità massima' (same top speed) is wrong: 110 is lower than 130.

sceneParams.caption: 110 km/h here, 130 km/h on motorways

q18362.en: Light quadricycles may travel on main out-of-town roads.

explain.short: Light quadricycles (small 'minicar' vehicles, max 45 km/h) are too slow. They are not allowed on these roads.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'quadricicli leggeri' (light quadricycles) are banned, like mopeds.

sceneParams.caption: Light quadricycles: not allowed here

q18363.en: Main out-of-town roads have only one lane in each direction.

explain.short: They must have at least two lanes in each direction.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'una sola corsia' (only one lane) is wrong: at least two lanes per direction.

sceneParams.caption: At least 2 lanes in each direction

q18364.en: Mopeds may travel on main out-of-town roads.

explain.short: Mopeds (ciclomotori, max 45 km/h) are too slow for these roads, so they are not allowed.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' (mopeds) are banned here.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds: not allowed here

q18365.en: On main out-of-town roads there are no bends or humps.

explain.short: Main out-of-town roads can have bends and humps like other roads. The definition says nothing against them.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'non vi sono curve né dossi' (no bends nor humps) is an invented claim.

sceneParams.caption: Bends and humps can exist on these roads too

q18366.en: Main out-of-town roads must be equipped with variable message panels.

explain.short: Electronic message panels are useful, but the law does not require them on these roads.
explain.rule: Main out-of-town road: separate carriageways, 2+ lanes each way, no level junctions, blue signs, limit 110 km/h, only some motor vehicles.
explain.trap: 'devono' (must) is the trap: these panels are not compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Message panels: possible, but not compulsory

q18367.en: A traffic island helps channel vehicles towards different directions.

explain.short: The island splits the traffic and guides each vehicle into the right lane for its direction.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'incanalamento' means channelling: guiding vehicles into lanes.

sceneParams.caption: The island guides cars into their directions

q18368.en: A traffic island is bordered by continuous white lines.

explain.short: The edge of a traffic island is a continuous white line. You must not cross it.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'strisce bianche continue' means continuous (solid) white lines.

sceneParams.caption: Edges: continuous white lines

q18369.en: A traffic island can be flush with the road or raised.

explain.short: Some islands are just painted on the road (flush). Others are raised, like a kerb.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'a raso' means flush (at road level); 'in rilievo' means raised.

sceneParams.caption: Painted (flush) or raised: both are islands

q18370.en: A traffic island is highlighted with white zebra stripes.

explain.short: White diagonal stripes (zebrature) show where the island is, so you can see it from far away.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'zebrature di colore bianco' means white zebra stripes (diagonal lines).

sceneParams.caption: White zebra stripes mark the island

q18371.en: A traffic island is a part of the road where motorcycles may not drive.

explain.short: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island, and motorcycles are vehicles too.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorcycles) are not an exception: the ban is for all vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Motorcycles too: no driving on the island

q18372.en: A flush traffic island is made of white zebra stripes.

explain.short: An island at road level is only painted: it is the area of white zebra stripes.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'a raso' (flush, at road level) means painted, not raised.

sceneParams.caption: Flush island = white zebra stripes on the road

q18373.en: A raised traffic island, if present, is preceded by white zebra stripes.

explain.short: Before a raised island there are white zebra stripes on the road. They warn you and guide you round it.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'preceduta da' means 'preceded by': the stripes come before the raised part.

sceneParams.caption: Zebra stripes before the raised island

q18374.en: A traffic island is a part of the road where vehicles may not drive.

explain.short: The island is there to guide traffic around it. No vehicle may drive over it.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'vietato il transito dei veicoli' (vehicles may not drive) is correct here.

sceneParams.caption: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island

q18375.en: A traffic island separates the carriageway from the hard shoulder.

explain.short: A traffic island guides traffic into different directions. The edge line separates the carriageway from the shoulder.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'separare la carreggiata dalla banchina' (separate carriageway and shoulder) is not its job.

sceneParams.caption: The island channels traffic; it is not a shoulder edge

q18376.en: A traffic island is for pedestrians to walk on.

explain.short: A traffic island is for guiding vehicles, not for pedestrians. Pedestrians use pavements and crossings.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'transito dei pedoni' (pedestrians walking) confuses it with a pavement or a pedestrian refuge.

sceneParams.caption: Island guides vehicles; it is not a walkway

q18377.en: A traffic island is a lay-by where vehicles can park.

explain.short: No vehicle may drive or park on a traffic island. A 'piazzola di sosta' is a lay-by, a different thing.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'piazzola di sosta' (lay-by) is something else entirely.

sceneParams.caption: Not a lay-by: no parking on the island

q18378.en: A traffic island may only be driven on by taxis and city buses.

explain.short: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island: there is no exception for taxis or buses.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'solo dai taxi e dagli autobus' invents an exception that does not exist.

sceneParams.caption: No exceptions: not even taxis or buses

q18379.en: A traffic island is the part of the city with the most traffic.

explain.short: A traffic island is a small part of the road that guides traffic. It is not a busy area of the city.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: The name 'isola di traffico' sounds like 'traffic area', but it is a road element.

sceneParams.caption: It is a road element, not a busy city area

q18380.en: A traffic island usually corresponds to the city's historic centre.

explain.short: A traffic island is part of the road layout. It has nothing to do with the historic centre.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'centro storico' (historic centre) is a trick: the island is just a road element.

sceneParams.caption: Not the historic centre: a road element

q18381.en: A traffic island is a lay-by for making U-turns.

explain.short: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island, so you cannot use it to turn round.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'inversione di marcia' (U-turn) is not what the island is for.

sceneParams.caption: No U-turns on the island: no vehicle on it

q18382.en: A traffic island is located outside the road.

explain.short: A traffic island is a part of the road itself, placed among the lanes.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'al di fuori della strada' (outside the road) is wrong: it is part of the road.

sceneParams.caption: The island is part of the road

q18383.en: A traffic island is for vehicles to stop on.

explain.short: You may not drive onto a traffic island, so you cannot stop on it either.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'fermata' (stopping) is not allowed on the island.

sceneParams.caption: No stopping on the island

q18384.en: A traffic island makes it easier for passengers to get on and off trams, trolleybuses and buses.

explain.short: That is a passenger island (salvagente / isola salvagente) at a stop. A traffic island only channels vehicles.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: Do not confuse 'isola di traffico' with the passenger island at tram and bus stops.

sceneParams.caption: That is the passenger island, not the traffic island

q18385.en: A traffic island is an area for parking vehicles.

explain.short: A traffic island is not a car park. No vehicle may drive or park on it.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio' (car park) is wrong: no vehicles are allowed on the island.

sceneParams.caption: Not a car park: no vehicles on the island

q18386.en: A traffic island is an urban pedestrian area.

explain.short: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is a zone closed to vehicles for people on foot. A traffic island is a road element that guides vehicles.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'area pedonale' (pedestrian area) is a completely different thing.

sceneParams.caption: Not a pedestrian area: it guides vehicles

q18387.en: A traffic island is a part of the road where mopeds may drive.

explain.short: No vehicle may drive on a traffic island, mopeds included.
explain.rule: A traffic island guides vehicles into different directions; it is marked with white zebra stripes or raised, and no vehicle may drive on it.
explain.trap: 'consentito il transito dei ciclomotori' (mopeds allowed) is wrong: no vehicle may pass.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds too: no driving on the island

q18388.en: A grade-separated intersection (junction) includes roads at different heights.

explain.short: In this junction one road passes over or under the other. They are at different heights.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'livelli sfalsati' means different levels; 'altezze diverse' means different heights: the same idea.

sceneParams.caption: Roads at different heights: one over the other

q18389.en: A grade-separated intersection (junction) makes traffic flow better, because it avoids vehicles crossing each other directly.

explain.short: Cars never cross paths at the same point, so they do not have to stop and wait for each other.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'esclude l'incrocio diretto' means vehicles never cross each other directly.

sceneParams.caption: No direct crossing, so traffic keeps flowing

q18390.en: A grade-separated intersection (junction) includes ramps, overpasses or underpasses.

explain.short: Ramps take you up or down; overpasses go over and underpasses go under the other road.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'rampe, sovrappassi o sottopassi' are ramps, overpasses or underpasses.

sceneParams.caption: Ramps, overpasses and underpasses

q18391.en: A grade-separated intersection (junction) has structures (ramps, overpasses, underpasses) linking roads at different levels.

explain.short: To go from one road to the other, you use ramps, overpasses or underpasses.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'infrastrutture' means built structures: here ramps, overpasses and underpasses.

sceneParams.caption: Ramps and bridges link the two levels

q18392.en: A grade-separated intersection is a level crossing between a road and the railway tracks.

explain.short: A crossing of road and railway at the same level is a level crossing (passaggio a livello). A grade-separated junction has roads at different heights.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'a raso' (at the same level) is the opposite of 'livelli sfalsati' (different levels).

sceneParams.caption: That is a level crossing, not a grade-separated junction

q18393.en: In a grade-separated intersection (junction), the general maximum speed limits do not apply.

explain.short: The general speed limits apply everywhere, junctions included. Ramps often have even lower limits.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'non valgono' (do not apply) is the trap: speed limits always apply.

sceneParams.caption: General speed limits still apply here

q18394.en: A grade-separated intersection (junction) is, as a rule, controlled by traffic lights.

explain.short: Vehicles never cross each other directly here, so traffic lights are normally not needed.
explain.rule: A grade-separated junction links roads at different heights with ramps, overpasses and underpasses, so vehicles never cross directly.
explain.trap: 'regolata da semafori' (controlled by traffic lights) is wrong: there is no direct crossing to control.

sceneParams.caption: No direct crossing, so no traffic lights needed
